public_sources: arXiv:2607.01640 AgentFlow: Building Agent Dependency Graphs for Static Analysis of Agent Programs
arXiv:2608.10502 From Faulty Memories to Corrected Actions: Dependency-Guided Rollback Repair for Memory-Augmented Agents

actions: Resolved sanitized control and role-local config before semantic work and froze the tuple after a repeated SHA-only head check.
Read only role-local continuation state and public sources.
Ran a deterministic SHA-256-seeded synthetic DAG study comparing runtime-local, runtime-plus-static union, scalar high-recall, global strict, class-aware strict, and whole-redraw rollback policies.
Separated per-surface completeness from global average recall and swept static false-positive overcapture.
Persisted a reproducible script and an immutable checkpoint with scope guards and a nonempty continuation frontier.
key_result: In the scoped synthetic model, a class-aware completeness contract preserves 100% recovery while avoiding some broad redraw when only dependency classes with complete contracts are present; a 0.97 global-average recall policy improves throughput only by accepting unrecovered stale-state cases. Static false positives remain primarily a replay-cost/blast-radius variable when true coverage is complete.
scope: Synthetic mechanism study only. Capture probabilities are invented and are not measured rates for AgentFlow, LangGraph, or production systems. Public papers support the failure-mode categories and provenance assumptions, not the synthetic numerical thresholds.
exact_next_action: Resolve and freeze the latest sanitized control first. Then relax the complete affected-component surface-inventory assumption by injecting unmodeled/custom dependency surfaces and class-correlated runtime/static misses; compare class-aware strict routing, fail-closed unknown-component redraw, and hybrid complements under matched replay cost before reintroducing source-verifier uncertainty.
